children: Russia’s S&P Global Composite PMI rose to 50.6 in August 2026 from 49.6 in the previous month, marking the highest reading since February and signalling the first expansion in private-sector activity in six months.
The upturn was driven by a renewed increase in services activity, which offset a further decline in manufacturing output.
However, demand conditions remained subdued, with new orders continuing to fall, albeit at only a fractional pace.
Weak demand also weighed on employment, prompting another round of job shedding across the private sector as firms reduced headcounts amid a further decline in outstanding business.
On the price front, overall input-cost inflation eased in August, while output charges across both manufacturers and service providers rose at faster rates.
Meanwhile, business confidence improved, with optimism about the private-sector outlook rising to its highest level since March.

title: Russia Private Sector Grows for First Time in 6 Months
